title: Enable Gradle builds on the Android editor via a dedicated build app
body:
This is an alternative to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104069

That PR communicates with Termux to run Gradle within Termux's Linux-like environment, whereas this PR communicates with a dedicated Android app that provides a custom Linux rootfs as the build environment for Gradle.

Using a dedicated app has the following pro's:

- There is no special setup the user needs to do - everything is included in the dedicated app to do Godot Gradle builds, whereas with Termux you need to do some setup to get all the right tools into your Termux environment
- The way Termux works can only work when targeting Android API 28 or lower; the dedicated app uses a different approach to providing a Linux-like environment that works even when targeting the latest Android API
- We looked at potentially integrating the build environment directly into Godot, so no external app would be needed at all, however, that has licensing issues. The dedicated app depends on GPL code to run it's Linux-like environment

Here's the current source code for the dedicated app:

https://github.com/godotengine/android-editor-buildenv-app

And here's a [pre-built APK](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YFTL-SsVAfx7zCS7_fmuA9cRL7kY5JOz/view?usp=sharing), since actually building that from source is kinda tricky (the normal Android parts are easy, but proot and the Android SDK build-tools need to be built from source too, and you need to run Docker to build the Linux rootfs).

And here's a (very sped up) video of running this on a Meta Quest 3:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=90xWoLvSPis

As one-time setup, you need to install the Linux rootfs in the build environment app, which takes a couple minutes, but you don't need to do that again, unless we update the rootfs (which we theoretically would only do for each new minor version of Godot). Also, at the moment, the rootfs is embedded in the APK. It would probably be better if it downloaded it off the internet - that would make the APK much smaller, and make it easier for us to update the rootfs.

The Gradle build took ~5 minutes in real world time. In theory, it should only take that long the first time, and could run much faster on subsequent runs. But at the moment, it completely cleans everything up after every build. This is something we could (and should!) definitely change, though

Closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13030
